utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Please be seated. Mr. Registrar, have the accused brought in, please. (The accused entered court).

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Let me say good morning to our friends the interpreters first, to make sure they can hear me well, as I hope everyone else can. Good morning Prosecution, good morning to the Defence. And without further delay, I give the floor to Mr. Nobilo, after, of course, having the Brigadier brought in.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Before we call in the Brigadier, we have an observation regarding the transcript yesterday. The Brigadier said that in Vitez municipality 521 HVO soldiers had been killed during the conflict with the BiH army, but the transcript said that 521 Croats were killed. These are figures relating only to soldiers. This figure relates only to soldiers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you for the clarification. It will be taken note of. (The witness entered court).

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Brigadier Slavko Marin, can you hear me.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mr. President, yes, I can, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Very well. Let us continue, then, Mr. Nobilo.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good morning, Brigadier. Yesterday we had just distributed a new document, but we didn't have time to discuss it, so I should like to ask the registrar to go back to that document and to give me the number, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document D348, 348A for the French version, 348B for the English version. It was not distributed, so we're going to distribute it now.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So, we have a document dated 27 January, 1993, "Implementation of the agreement on unconditional cessation of hostilities." Order issued by Colonel Tihomir Blaskic. "Further to the agreement reached at the meeting with representatives of BH army mediated by the United Nations, the deputy commander of the United Nations forces in Bosnia and Herzegovina, Brigadier Simpson, on the 27th of January, 1993, and the order of the supreme commander of the HVO, of the HZHB, and in order to fully implement all the provisions I hereby order:" And I shall read only the key points. Point 1: Execute the implementation of the cessation of hostilities and establish a cease-fire involving all types of weapons. 2. Allow the UNPROFOR representatives to monitor the cease-fire. 3. Allow the unhindered and safe passage of all vehicles and personnel of UNPROFOR, the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees and other humanitarian organisations. Responsible for the execution of this order, military police commander and chief of police department. Deadline for execution: immediately. 4. Guarantee the safety of the vehicles and personnel of UNPROFOR, the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees and the International Committee of the Red Cross in the zone of responsibility of HVO brigades in the Operational Zone of Central Bosnia, warning them of any potential danger during passage --"

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: We're having a problem with the monitor, Judge, it's not coming up on the monitor. I don't know if it's coming up on anyone else's monitor. The actual item that counsel has on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Does the public gallery have the document? Can they see the document?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Looks like they have it. I think they have it, but it's not coming up on ours, Judge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: The Judges have it on their video.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: There is indeed a minor technical problem, it is not possible to see the document on the computer monitor, but we do have it on the screen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Kehoe, can you make do with that?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, it has come up on the screen. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Fine, thank you. Please continue, Mr. Nobilo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So, I'll go back to point 4. "Guarantee the safety of the vehicles and personnel of UNPROFOR, the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees and the International Committee of the Red Cross in the zone of responsibility of HVO brigades in the Central Bosnia Operative Zone, warning them of any potential danger during transit through territories affected by offensive activities of BH army units. 5. Allow exchange of all prisoners through the office of the International Committee of the Red Cross. Brigadier, we will not go on reading this document, because it may not be so relevant for our case, but I would like to ask you to tell the Court whether you recollect the content of this order.

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: Mr. President, Your Honours, I do recall the contents and activities ordered in this document. The content itself speaks about the tasks of the units on the ground, and further, to the agreement reached on a cessation of hostilities between HVO units and BH army troops.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Brigadier, will you tell the Court, we see here for the first time that the commander, Colonel Tihomir Blaskic, has not signed this document. How was this document dispatched, and to whom?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: From the text of the document it is clear that the document was drafted in the command of the Operative Zone, that it was typed on a computer, and that it was sent by packet link to the Chief of Staff of the main headquarters, all HVO brigades and independent units in the Operational Zone of Central Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please look at point 9, and the last sentence, where it says that a commission is appointed consisting of Franjo Nakic and Ivica Zeko, and it also says that instructions for the meeting will be provided later. Where was Colonel Blaskic on the 27th of January, and where were Nakic and Zeko on that date?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: As far as I recall, on the 27th of January, Blaskic was in Kiseljak, because, due to the January conflicts in the territory of Busovaca, or more specifically in the area of Kacuni, the Kacuni-Busovaca-Kiseljak road was intersected and placed under the control of the BH army, and this road was no longer passable by the HVO. That is why this sentence is there saying that instructions will be provided later, probably when he has occasion to meet personally with Franjo Nakic and Ivica Zeko. Franjo Nakic, as the Chief of Staff, was in Vitez at the time, I was with him. And Ivica Zeko was in Bila where his department was headquartered.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How did you communicate with Colonel Blaskic in January?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: In January when the conflict occurred in the territory of Busovaca municipality, and the conflict between HVO units and BH army units in Busovaca and a part of Kiseljak municipality, General Blaskic was on the territory of Kiseljak municipality the night before. As far as I know, he went to his family home in the village of Brestovsko, where he was born, and which is situated on the territory of Kiseljak municipality. Colonel Blaskic would go home to spend the night occasionally in the past, too. When the road was cut at Kacuni and placed under BH army control, General Blaskic stayed behind in Kiseljak. Under those conditions we communicated in the following manner: Information that we received from the ground from brigade commanders, and which were received in the command of the Operative Zone, we would study those reports, and the parts that we thought General Blaskic should be familiarised with, we would send them by packet to the command of the Ban Jelicic Brigade, and from there it reached General Blaskic. Typical for that period was that information reached General Blaskic with a great deal of delay. Why? Because they were late in coming from brigade commanders in Busovaca, Vitez, Novi Travnik and Travnik, in the command. And then we would have to process those documents, establish contact with Kiseljak; so this would take time, and this information reached General Blaskic late. It is also noteworthy that at that time we knew that our communications were being tapped, that our reports may be seen by the enemy, so, we had to limit the scope of the reports we sent to General Blaskic. This meant that under conditions of poor communications, insecure links, he did not have timely, nor completely accurate information as to what was happening in the area of Busovaca and the Lasva Valley.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Brigadier. Next document, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document D349, D349A for the French version, D349B for the English version.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We have another order of Colonel Blaskic's dated the 27th of January, 1993, and it is headed "Passage of humanitarian aid convoys." The order reads, in point one, I'm only citing what is relevant. "All vehicles and convoys carrying humanitarian aid to be let through only if escorted by a) the United Nations, b) the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees. Commander Tihomir Blaskic." Brigadier, at the time you were in the headquarters of the Central Bosnia Operative Zone, you said that the colonel was in Kiseljak; do you recall this order? Was it agreed upon with Colonel Blaskic? Did he give you permission to issue such an order?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: Yes, I recall that the activities that we had to undertake, as referred to in the text of this order, so, this order is just a follow-up in relation to previous ones regarding the cessation of hostilities and the normalisation of conditions in the area of Central Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Next document, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document D350, D350A for the French version, 350B for the English version.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the 31st of January, 1993, the commander of the Central Bosnia Operative Zone, Colonel Tihomir Blaskic, is writing to Mr. Mustafa Agic, and the subject of the letter is "Apology for the brutal behaviour of extremist members of the HVO in Kiseljak. Dear Sir, I have been informed by the competent authorities about the destructive behaviour of an uncontrolled group of HVO soldiers, who, on the 29th of January, 1993, between 1400 and 1600 hours, demolished your catering establishment. I'm aware of the fact that this kind of behaviour in the HVO by extremists undermines the situation and creates distrust among the inhabitants of Kiseljak regarding their personal safety, but I can promise you that appropriate measures will be taken against the perpetrators of these acts. I wish to apologise to you once again for everything that was done by the extremists within the ranks of the HVO. Regards, Commander of the Central Bosnia Operative Zone, Colonel Tihomir Blaskic." Brigadier, do you remember this incident, and Colonel Blaskic's apology to Mustafa Agic?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: I do not exactly remember the incident, but I do remember this apology. This is Colonel Blaskic's signature, but the stamp is of the Josipa Ban Jelacic Brigade, which means the commander is still in Kiseljak.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the stamp is from Kiseljak?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There is no communication centre stamp or reference number?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: Yes, because he was in Kiseljak.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell us what nationality was Mustafa Agic?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: He is a Muslim Bosniak.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is this letter typical of Colonel Blaskic and such an attitude on the part of a commander towards the owner of a cafe? Was it customary, or was it an exception in the territory of Central Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: May I comment on this letter? Whenever General Blaskic had complete and timely information about an event, he would react immediately so as to try and deal with the problem, if the information was correct and complete. And this apology is a case in point. The commander of the Operative Zone, General Blaskic, who had the level of a two-star general, in such a very difficult situation after a conflict, after we had had so many casualties, and the fact that we could not pass through Kacuni, in spite of all these problems, he found it necessary to apologise to Mustafa Agic because of the vandalism committed by extremists within HVO ranks. So, this is also an illustration of General Blaskic's character and his personality and his professionalism at work. So, such incidents as destruction of catering establishments in Central Bosnia during the war were quite frequent on all sides, both on the side of the HVO units, the BH army units and members of the Republika Srpska army.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. We may have caused some hesitation among the Judges. You said that Blaskic was a two-star general. Was he indeed a two-star general at the time, or was he performing duties that were equivalent to those of a two-star general?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: When I mentioned a two-star general, what I wished to say was the very high level of the position General Blaskic held. And in spite of such a superior position that he had, he had time to think about an individual, in spite of such very grave problems surrounding us. So, he found the time to address this individual, to apologise to him, and to offer him guarantees that he would take steps to make his life safer. That's what I wanted to say.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Nobilo, that was a good explanation.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Next document, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document D351, D351A for the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Mr. President, we will now read the next document.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It is a joint document of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, the 3rd Corps command and the command of the Central Bosnia Operative Zone. It was drafted in Kakanj on the 13th of February, 1993, and the subject heading is "Free passage for convoys and transports." Colonel Tihomir Blaskic, commander of the Central Bosnia Operative Zone and the commander of the 3rd Corps, Enver Hadzihasanovic, jointly are issuing an order, and I will only read what I consider two relevant points. 1. Immediately enable all convoys that have been stopped to depart for their destinations with all of their cargo. 2. Ensure the unhindered passage of all convoys with papers that are in order, especially those going to the RBH army and the HVO units of the Croatian community of Herceg-Bosna, and also for convoys of humanitarian aid. Signed by Hadzihasanovic and Blaskic. Do you recognise the stamp of the Operative Zone and Colonel Blaskic's signature?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, how were these documents drafted? How did it happen that both Hadzihasanovic and Blaskic are giving orders through the same document?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: Mr. President, Your Honours, we can see the following from this document: That this situation and the control of security and traffic, both in the area under HVO control, as well as in the area under BiH army control, was eschewing full control. What does that mean? It means that incidents occurred, and certain groups would stop transports arbitrarily, whether they were transports of humanitarian aid or other transports. And in view of these occurrences, and to deal with the problem and ensure unhindered passage of convoys and transports through territory under BH army control and under HVO control, the commander of the 3rd Corps, together with the commander of the Operative Zone are issuing the same order to both the HVO units and BH army units. So, this is a clear reflection of the complexity of the situation, and of the effort that was required and the perseverance that was required to make life normal.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We received this document from the Prosecutor's office. But tell us, this document was signed by two key commanders of the BH army and the HVO. Were such orders always carried out, or were there problems, nevertheless?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: In spite of such clear, concrete, specific orders, problems would occur. And this made it necessary for the commander of both the 3rd Corps and of the Operative Zone to issue a series of other orders, and we will probably be seeing some of them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there instances of disobedience on both sides, equally?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: In such cases, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the main reason for the lack of immediate respect for an order of this kind?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: The key reason was the one I referred to on the first day of my testimony, and that is the lack of a firm structure, both in the HVO and in the BH army, arbitrariness on the part of individuals and groups.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Next document, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document D352, 352A for the English version.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So, this is another document which we received from the office of the Prosecutor. It is a joint order, again, or command. This is the commander of the 3rd Corps and the Operative Zone of Central Bosnia of 13 February, 1993, and it's regarding the withdrawal of units from positions. The pertinent point is 1. The immediate withdrawal of units from lines of contact, all units from other municipalities shall immediately return to the territories of those municipalities. First let's try to clarify something for the Judges. It says order and then command, and then it says unit, and then it uses the Croatian word for unit, which is postrojba. Why is this done in this manner?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: Since this is a joint document which was signed by the commanders of the Operative Zone and of the 3rd Corps, we are using two languages. We Croats, for order, use the word Zapovijed. And they use the word Naredjenje, which is also order. We use Postrojba for a unit and the Bosniaks use Jedinica. So these are all different words in two different languages. And it was done in this manner so it would be acceptable to both parties so that both the Bosniak and the Croatian version were used.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell me, what are the other units that are being mentioned here, that is units from the other municipalities?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: As I see that this document was drafted on 13 February, which means after the conflicts in Busovaca and Kiseljak municipalities, I assume that this refers to the units which had arrived to this area from other municipalities. So this could be units from Kakanj, which were involved on the attack on Busovaca and they were supposed to have been withdrawn. And if they had come from Zenica then they would have had to withdraw from there. And if they were the units from Novi Travnik and they were engaged in Busovaca, they would have had to have withdrawn.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So these are all units that were within the state of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Brigadier, do you know whether a joint command was operative based on these documents and that their commanders were Colonel Blaskic and Enver Hadzihasanovic?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: In this period and yesterday we saw that after the conflict in April of 1993, that is after the cessation of hostilities, there was always an idea present and a desire, at least on the part of the Central Bosnia Operative Zone commander, as well as some higher commanders in the BH army as well as the HVO, to establish a joint command of the BH army and the HVO in order to coordinate the defence against the army of the Republika Srpska. However, in view of the conflicts of January and then in April, 1993, and then June, all these conflicts prevented this joint command for ever becoming to life.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell the Judges what was the position of General Blaskic regarding the conflict of Muslims at that time, especially in view of the larger conflict with Serbs?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: General Blaskic, did not want a conflict with the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina and I think that we reviewed at least a hundred documents here. I also recall his oral orders. He never ever ordered an attack against the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina. All his activities were defensive in their nature and I think that we have been proving this as long as I have been sitting here and this is a generally known fact in Central Bosnia and in the territory which was under the control of the Central Bosnia Operative Zone.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Next document, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: D353, D353A for the English version.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This is another document which we received from the Office of the Prosecutor and another document referring to the joint command. It was drafted in Kakanj on 13 February, 1992, and the subject heading is "Return of population to their homes." It was addressed to all the Central Bosnia Operative Zone HVO Brigades, to dependent units, to the military police battalion and so on. I am only going to read the relevant parts. "That the conditions should be created for the return of refugee population to their homes. The population returning to their homes should be guaranteed complete security, unimpeded and safe movement shall be assured for the whole population throughout the free territory." And then it was signed by commander of the 3rd Corps, Enver Hadzihasanovic, and commander of the HVO Central Bosnian Operative Zone, Colonel Tihomir Blaskic. Colonel, do you recall this document?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: I recall very well all activities which were directed at cessation of the hostilities. But I also recall a fact that I would like to point out here. Here in Item 1, it states that the conditions should be created for the return of the refugee population to their homes. The conflict between the HVO and the BH army occurred. What happened in this conflict was that the population of both sides were fleeing. The Croatian population was fleeing from the areas which was coming under the BH army control and vice versa. And this is why the commander of the 3 Corps and the commander of the Central Bosnia Operative Zone are ordering their units to allow the civilian population to come back and not to prevent the population from returning to their homes and to provide full safety in order for them to be able to continue with their normal lives.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Next document, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document D354, 354A for the English version.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I will first read the text and then analyse it. On 19 February, 1993, at 1955 hours, commander of the Operative Zone, Colonel Tihomir Blaskic, is writing to the commander of the 4th military police battalion. And part of the page is damaged, but it is about the security situation in prison. "On the basis of a report from the relevant service and people in charge of" -- and the date is not legible -- but it's "1993 at 1245, and with the aim of preventing the same and similar activities, I hereby order: Submit a detailed report on the break in of your members into the Busovaca military prison on the 2nd and 16th February, 1993, at 2200 hours respectively when the group committed the following: A) forcible entry into the military prison under the threat of the use arms. B) forcible taking of prisoners from their cells." "As I know for certain that these were members of the military police and the intervention platoon and the security service of the prison knows who these men were, I am drawing your attention -- I direct you to inform your subordinates once again and forbid such actions and take the necessary measures against the perpetrators." "The following are responsible for the execution of the order: Nikola Subic-Zrinjski Brigade commander, Mr. Dusko Grubesic, 4th military police battalion commander, Mr. Pasko Ljubicic," and the deadline for the execution of the order is 26th February, ‘93 by 1200 hours of "which I shall be informed in writing and the signature is Central Bosnia Operative Zone commander, Tihomir Blaskic." Brigadier, do you recall this incident?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: I recall that this order was issued after the information reached General Blaskic that these activities are as spelled out in this report occurred in the prison. I do not know about the event itself, but this order confirms, regardless of the nature of the incident, it confirms that the information came to reach General Blaskic in a timely fashion and he took steps to resolve it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When was this document drafted?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: This was on the 19th of February and that means that General Blaskic was still in Kiseljak at that time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We also have traces of a stamp, is this the stamp, the usual stamp that was used?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: It should be, but it is not fully visible, so I cannot really say.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We see that the military police had broken into the prison forcibly and Colonel Blaskic is demanding of the military police commander to take disciplinarian measures, why did Mr. Blaskic not himself punish the perpetrators?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: I mentioned that before that the Operative Zone commander did not have authority over the military police and could not get involved in the disciplinary measures.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Next document, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: D355, D355A for the English version.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This document was also received from the Office of the Prosecutor and it is another joint order that is command of the 3rd Corps commander, Mr. Hadzihasanovic, and the commander of the Operative Zone, Tihomir Blaskic. It is dated 13 February, 1993 and the subject heading is: "Discharge of imprisoned and detained persons." I will read three items: "One, that all imprisoned and detained persons be released unconditionally and immediately by 1200 hours on 15th February 1993 at the latest. The only persons from your own information who have breached rules, regulations and laws may be continue to be held in detention prison. And three, that all released persons be guaranteed complete freedom and security to be provided by the municipal defence headquarters and the municipal defence office." And Hadzihasanovic and Blaskic signed this order. Can you tell me, do you recall this joint command order? Did it reach you? Did it reach the HVO command?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: I completely recall this order and the tasks. It is clear from the order that it was sent to all the HVO brigades, but it also shows that there were imprisoned and detained persons who were the HVO members and who were arrested by the BH army and there were BH army soldiers who were detained by the HVO. So, both commanders are ordering their units to release these persons and that the persons, those members of the HVO should remain who had breached rules and laws should remain in detention. So they are releasing the other-side soldiers and they're keeping their own and it is referring to the soldiers to whom the HVO had given certain disciplinarian punishment.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document D356, D356A for the English version.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This document was also provided by the Office of the Prosecutor, another joint command order of the 3rd Corps commander and the Operative Zone commander and it's subject, heading is, "Removal of the road barricades," and I am going to read the first paragraph. "All barricades and obstacles shall be removed from all communication routes to ensure an unimpeded flow of two-way traffic." Is this another document which resulted from the cessation of hostilities?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: Yes, this is also in the spirit of implementation of the cease-fire agreement.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Next document, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 357, 357A for the French version, 357B for the English version.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This is an order issued by Blaskic alone. That is the Operative Zone commanders' order of 11 March, 1993, at 1255 hours and it is to the commander of the 4th Battalion of the military police in Vitez. It regards treatment of foreigners. "On the 10th of March, 1993, at 1100 hours, members of the military police in Vitez detained Mr. Abdulah Jusuf from Kuwait according to the statement from the written protest No. 02/33-649 of 10 March, 1993, sent in by the commander of the 3rd Corps of the army of BH in Zenica. Because a number of failures are quoted in the protest, I order: One, complete investigation of this case is to be conducted. Establish who arrived in a red van mentioned in the report 02-4/3-07 of 10 March, '93. Return the money and motor vehicles to the taxi driver and obtain from him a signed receipt. Four, propose disciplinarian measures against persons who have committed this misdemeanour and implement them. And, five, the deadline for this order is 11 March, '93." Brigadier, do you recall this?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: Yes, I do. This document was signed by Colonel Blaskic. It was drafted by Mr. Blaskic and it bears the stamp of the Operative Zone command.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know anything more about this? There is something in handwriting here and it could be his handwriting as far as I know. It says something like, lie confirmed, and it is signed by Blaskic?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: It is not fully legible. But I also would make out the word "lie." And I think I also recognise his signature there. However, what is important here is this document confirms that General Blaskic, when he would receive information in a timely fashion, he would immediately take appropriate steps. We can see that this was in response to the 3rd Corps commanders' memo to General Blaskic and we see the measures and we see what General Blaskic is ordering in Items 1 through 5.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Next document, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 358, D358A for the English version.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Therefore, the next document has also come to us from the Prosecutor's office. It is entitled, "Ensuring the unobstructed movement of representatives of the European Monitoring Mission." And commander Tihomir Blaskic signed the document from the Central Bosnia Operative Zone dated 18th of March, 1993. And point one states: First, "I order that the unobstructed passage of the representatives of the European Monitoring Mission be ensured on all roads in the zone of responsibility of the units of the HVO Operative Zone, Central Bosnia Croatian Defence Council. Two, that the personnel manning the checkpoints: A) Establish and take note of the signs on the motor vehicles of the monitoring mission without halting the motor vehicles; B) Approve the passage of motor vehicles carrying monitors without halting them at checkpoints." Brigadier, do you recall the problems that you had with the passage of monitoring missions and humanitarian organisations and how did Blaskic react and what did he do to ensure international organisations, especially international humanitarian organisation, safe and unobstructed passage?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: The contents from this order I recall very well. The document was signed by General Blaskic. This document was drafted in the aim of implementing the signed agreements and the creation of possibilities for the unobstructed passage and movement of international humanitarian organisations and representatives of the European Monitoring Mission. As I said a moment ago when I explained the documents signed by General Blaskic and the commander of the 3rd Corps, Enver Hadzihasanovic, that the problem with regard to movement along roads controlled by HVO units and BH army units, that problems did exist and in endeavour to overcome them, concrete measures and orders were given. Clear cut orders. This order speaks of a persistent endeavour on the part of General Blaskic to adhere to all the undertaken agreements made and to issue orders to his subordinates to implement them fully in the field.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Brigadier, is that the signature of the Colonel Blaskic?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: Yes, it is. It is a paper of the operations and training body. I don't know what the number is in the upper right-hand corner, 0055 and so on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That is the reference number of the Prosecutor's Office. May we move on now, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The next document is D359, 359A for the French version and 359B for the English version.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We have another order from Colonel Blaskic --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: The public gallery, as regards the systemic presentation of documents. Thank you. We have it on the monitor. Each document shown to be flashed for the benefit of the public. Thank you. And then, obviously, the camera will be moving around as it wishes. But the public must see the document that we are discussing because this is a public hearing. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. But technology is in the hands of the technical service of the Trial Chamber and the Court, so we are not able to direct it ourselves fully.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: I am not blaming absolutely anyone, not even our friends in the technical booth. I am just saying what I consider to be important for the proper proceedings.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President, the public is very important to us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Brigadier, we have an order by Colonel Blaskic dated the 22nd of April, 1993, to all the Brigade commanders, commanders of the independent units, the 4th LTR, tank division and so on. "Treatment of citizens, personal property order: In order to stop arson attacks on houses and business premises, as well as the looting of property, I hereby order: On the territory of the area of responsibility of the Central Bosnia Operative Zone command controlled by the HVO units -- and now it is written in capital letters -- I MOST STRICTLY FORBID the torching of houses, and business premises and the looting of property. The commanders of brigades and independent units must issue this order to their subordinates and make them responsible for stopping such misdeeds. Those who act in violation of this order are to be subject to the strictest measures in line with the rules on military discipline in the HVO units. The contents of this order should have been made known to all members of the HVO units and the media is to be used in this regard too. This order shall take effect immediately and the commanders of Brigades and independent units of the Central Bosnia Operative Zone responsible to me for its execution, Commander Colonel Tihomir Blaskic." Brigadier, tell me first, please, whether this photocopy is an authentic representation of the original order issued by Tihomir Blaskic on the 22nd of April, 1993?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: Yes, I recall the text in full. I personally wrote the order and it was signed by the commander Tihomir Blaskic of the Operative Zone.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Brigadier, what was the reason for issuing this order stopping the arson attacks on houses; is that not generally prohibited?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: In conflicts, the conflicts that occurred in the area of the Lasva River Valley, the responsibility zone of Central Bosnia between the units of the HVO and the army, that is to say, in conflicts of this kind, there were instances where houses were set fire to, in the area controlled by the HVO, but also in the area controlled by the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina. When the commander of the Operative Zone came across information of this kind and saw that this was happening in the field, in order to stop incidents of this kind, that is to prevent them from taking place, he most strictly issued this order and emphasised it was most strictly forbidden to do this kind of thing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, Brigadier, according to the best of your knowledge, did Colonel Blaskic ever order civilian houses to be burned, or did he ever give the okay for somebody else to do this?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: General Blaskic never acquiesced to anything of this kind, nor did he ever issue such orders. The burning of houses is the results of individual activity, that is, the activities of individuals who performed acts of this kind, and not only of this kind, but other acts, as well, which we have mentioned in the documents that we are presenting here today.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So, this order was issued, we see on the 22nd of April, which means it was one day after the return from Zenica by Colonel Blaskic when he had talks with the representatives of the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. May I have the next document, please?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document D360, D360A for the French version, 360B for the English version.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The next order, Comrade Blaskic, commander of the Operative Zone, was issued on the 23rd of April, 1993, at 2000 hours. It is entitled "The behaviour of HVO members and the level of military discipline." And it is intended and addressed to all subordinate HVO commanders. The preamble reads as follows: "Because a very strong condemnation from the International Community and a media campaign that is being conducted against the HVO and Croatian people, which have extremely negative consequences on the overall reputation of the HVO and the achievements of the Croatian people globally, and in order to prevent further destructive activities and fully implement the orders of the chief of the HVO main headquarters, I hereby order: 1. Execute the order number 01-4-470/93 of the 21st of April, 1993, in full. Responsible: Directly supporting commanders. Deadline: Immediately. 2. Ensure the full and unhindered passage of U.N. vehicles and the ECMM vehicles, greeting them with the proper HVO military salute. Responsible: Directly subordinate commanders. Deadline: Immediately. 3. Once again, I urge you to behave in the most military fashion and respect military discipline. Legal measures should be taken against those violating this order. 4. I strictly forbid all HVO units to carry out offensive actions, and isolated provocations by the BH army are not to be responded to. 5. To open fire only in case of direct attack by Muslim forces, but only following an order issued by the superior commanders, about which the brigade commanders must inform me immediately. 6. This order shall take effect immediately. Colonel Tihomir Blaskic." Brigadier, do you remember this order? Do you know the stamp and sign, and is it an authentic representation of the original document?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: Yes, it is. It is an authentic photocopy of the original document. I recall the text of the order. It was written personally by General Blaskic. The stamp is the stamp of the Operative Zone, and it was, as I say, personally written by General Blaskic, himself.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, please, let us take a look at point two. What was the problem? Because we see that there is a problem of the passage of international organisations and their vehicles, and the conduct at control points with regard to the U.N. vehicles. What was the problem there?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: Well, the problem occurred in the following way: Individuals without authorisation from anybody, independently and autonomously, working on their own free will and own assessment, in parts of the roads, would stop vehicles belonging to international organisations and European monitoring missions, and their conduct was not as it should have been, and their conduct towards them overstepped the boundaries of the orders issued to them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Brigadier, is it correct that Blaskic issued certain orders and prohibitions when he found something to be a problem? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: Yes, we have borne this out with all the orders issued so far. I said this before, and I'm saying it again: General Blaskic, whenever he had the opportunity and had timely information, did not wait one second or one minute, he would take action immediately, and take measures to solve the problem.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Brigadier, take a look at point 4, if you will, please, when Blaskic forbids the carrying out of offensive actions, and in item 5, when he forbids anybody to open fire unless attacked; does that mean that somebody opened fire on the part of the HVO without having orders to do so?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: Individual cases, when fire was opened by soldiers in the trenches was done without permission and without orders of the commander of the Operative Zone and their brigades. In order to prevent activities of this kind, that means that the general issued orders as points 4 and points 5 read. However, if there were individual instances of behaviour of this kind by irresponsible HVO members, I must say that the same existed on the Bosnian side, the side of the Bosnian army. So, it is stated here that there were individual provocations by the BH army and we saw this from the documents we read out yesterday after the signing of the cease-fire. So, in situations of this kind, General Blaskic prohibited that forces open fire, but asked that he be informed of incidents of this kind, and then via his various links, he would contact the commander of the 3rd Corps and solve problems of this nature.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We see here that Blaskic is calling for disciplinary measures to be taken, and the title of the document was "The behaviour of HVO members and the level of military discipline." Can you explain to the Court what links there are with the level of military discipline with the incidents that Blaskic saw were happening in the field and which prompted him to issue orders of this kind? What is the link between the level of military discipline with these incidents?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: Well, they are directly linked, and if you have a poor level of organisation and military discipline, then you will have incidents of this kind. If you have a good level of organisation and very good military discipline, these incidents are practically impossible. And that is why General Blaskic, in his orders and in the work he did under wartime conditions, constantly endeavoured to build-up a high level of organisation and military discipline. Because once this structure was built-up and once you had the necessary level of organisation and military discipline, all the incidents would not take place; which means there would be no need to issue orders of this kind. So any kind of conduct of this kind towards international organisations and improper conduct would have been avoided and suppressed; and that is why, for these reasons, in the course of his entire work, right up to the Washington Agreement, and further on after it, General Blaskic placed the accent on organisation and professional military discipline, because he knew if he had good discipline and good organisation that he would have good units and his orders would be implemented on location.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Mr. President, we have a new document, if you would like to make a break now, this might be a good time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: We're going to have a 20-minute break now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: The hearing is resumed. Have the accused brought in, please. (The accused entered court).

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Nobilo, your witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Would you hand round the new document, please?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 361, D361A for the French version, D361B for the English version.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Brigadier, I think that this is one of the most severe orders issued by Blaskic, and I'm going to read it out carefully and will comment on it point by point. The Central Bosnia Operative Zone, and it is an order the 24th of April, 1993, at 0920 hours to all commanders of all units in the Central Bosnia Operative Zone. The title is "The elimination of arbitrary acts by commanders and individuals." Preamble: "After an assessment carried out in the field, it is apparent that the lower commanders and their units are acting outside the chain of command. They are not executing orders from superiors, and are independently making decisions contrary to the orders received. They plan and execute their own combat activities. They plan and execute their own combat activities, exert pressure on civilians and disrupt the work of UNPROFOR, the International Red Cross and the European Monitoring Mission in performing their duties, which has negative consequences for the HVO and those soldiers who execute the received tasks consistently. In order to eliminate these negative actions and to execute fully the order of the commander, the chief of the HVO main headquarters, 01-1583/93 on the 22nd of April, 1993, I hereby order: 1. Warn all the levels of command of the enormous negative impact of such behaviour by individuals and groups, especially in the international arena. 2. All the organised troops are to be fully controlled and the commanders are personally responsible for the behaviour of their subordinates. 3. The individuals and groups who are completely out of control are to be arrested immediately, and warrants are to be delivered to the commander of the military police unit. 4. You are in charge of preventing the most extremists individuals and groups who are out of control, who are not protecting the civilians, who are demolishing and setting fire to civilian facilities, and whose activities are none other than terrorism, with all available means and with the use of force. 5. Against all those who are disrupting the mission of UNPROFOR, the UNHCR and the ECMM and the ICRC, the International Red Cross, the most stringent measures are to be taken, as this is the fight for the reputation and dignity of the HVO and the Croatian people and the Croatian community of Herceg-Bosna. All these organisations have complete freedom of movement and you are duty bound to assist them in their activities. 6. In order to fulfil these tasks, the directly subordinate commanders are responsible to me, as well as for the practical application of this order, and I make all the command and control responsible for this." And it is signed by the commander, Colonel Tihomir Blaskic. Brigadier, do you recall this order, and do you recognise the stamp and signature of Colonel Blaskic?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: I remember the contents of the order, it was personally signed by General Blaskic and written by General Blaskic, and the stamp is that of the command of the Operative Zone.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are the contents and the assessment of the situation given by Blaskic in the preamble, in the first part, and then later on, in prohibiting certain conduct, is it a reflection of the actual situation in the field in Central Bosnia in April, 1993?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: Yes. And I should particularly like to emphasise the first sentence in the preamble. "After an assessment carried out in the field, and issuing orders which were designed to stop the negative incidents and control of their implementation," as is stated in the preamble.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it true that the lower commanders and their units and subordinates were acting arbitrarily?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: Yes, and this that is why this order expressly defines who is responsible and who must prevent negative behaviour and incidents of this kind.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it true what is stated in line 3, that these subordinates are making individual decisions themselves, contrary to orders issued by their superiors; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We need not go further in analysing the order, it speaks for itself. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document D362, 362A for the French version, 362B for the English version.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Colonel Blaskic, on the 24th of April, 1993, at 1000, issues an order entitled, "Treatment of the wounded," and I'm going to read the two relevant points of that order. 1. "Unhindered access and rendering assistance to all wounded persons, be they civilians, soldiers or enemy soldiers is to be ensured. 2. Civilians and prisoners are to be treated in accordance with international conventions and regulations, and lists containing names of those taken prisoner or being detained are to be immediately provided to the Central Bosnia Operational Zone. Immediately subordinate commanders are responsible to me in connection with carrying out this order." Signed, Lieutenant Colonel Blaskic. Brigadier, do you recognise the stamp and signature on this document and do you recall the order itself?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: Yes, I do, I remember the contents, because it was based on a decision by the head of the chief of the general staff. I know the provisions. It was signed by General Blaskic. The document was authorised in the central zone and was personally signed by Colonel Blaskic. From the text it can be clearly seen what was to be done in the field.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. The next document, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document D363, 363A for the French version, 363B for the English version.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Once again, an order from Colonel Blaskic, issued on the 24th of April, 1993, at 1100 a.m., and it refers to a series of commanders; Busovaca, Kiseljak, the police force department, Vitez, the police station of the Croatian community, et cetera. And it is the relationship towards housing resources and property and flats. "Because of a large number of flats temporarily vacant which are being forced into by persons carrying arms, soldiers of the HVO and other persons, in order to enforce public order and peace in the town of Vitez, as well as to prevent such negative developments..." and then in writing, with a red pen, he adds: "and other towns, I hereby order: 1. That all resources should be used, and that the use of force resorted to in the unlawful taking of flats and stealing of property from the flats which belong to citizens who for different reasons are temporarily not present. And it is the commander of the 4th Battalion of the Croatian Defence Council, military police and commanders of the stations of the Croatian community of Herceg-Bosna who are responsible to me, personally, for carrying out this order. The order comes into effect immediately. And as regards the members of the Croatian Defence Council carrying uniforms, they will be subject to measures implemented by the Croatian Defence Council and military police, while civilians will be subject to the civil police of the Croatian community of Herceg-Bosna, those two working in coordination." Signed by Colonel Blaskic. Tell me, please, Brigadier, whether this photocopy is an authentic representation of the original; did you see the original when it was written?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: Yes, the photocopy is a reflection of the original. The document was written and signed by General Blaskic, and the stamp is the Operative Zone. And the tasks set out in the order I recall very well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Brigadier, would you look at point 1, and the last line of point 1, where Colonel Blaskic speaks of empty flats, that is to say, empty flats of citizens who, for different reasons, are temporarily not present. Tell the Court, please, what ethnic group were the people that left Vitez, temporarily, in the section which was under the control of the HVO?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: Temporarily, absent individuals were the Muslims, the Bosniaks, as well as some Croats and some Serbs. But for the most part, the majority of citizens who were absent were the Muslims, the Bosniaks; because they had left, they had escaped following the conflict between the HVO and BH army.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And tell me, how did Blaskic treat those Bosniaks who had left Vitez? Did he consider they had left for good, or did they consider that when the situation calmed down again these people would return? What do you remember from talking to him in that regard?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: General Blaskic always considered that this was a temporary state, and that the people who had escaped under different conditions and circumstances would come back to their own houses, and that is clearly seen from the sentence which states "are temporarily not present."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Brigadier, they entered your flat as well when you were away for three days, temporarily?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: Yes, at that time, as I have already stated, I spent some time in Vitez on assignment and I did not come home. My wife was visiting with her parents, with the children, and when I came back home, I found other people in my flat. So I had to solve this problem myself, regardless of the fact that I was well-known to people in the town and that I performed the functions that I performed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Next document, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document D364, 364A for the French version, 364B for the English version.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Another order by Colonel Blaskic of 24 April, '93, at 1420 hours. It was issued to all HVO units, including Brigades and the independent units and the subject heading is "Treatment of civilians and prisoners." And the body of text runs as follows: "On the basis of the request from the Chief of main headquarters No. 02-2/1-01-673/93 of 22 April, '93, and with regard to the application of the basic principles of international humanitarian law by all units and members of the HVO, I hereby demand: 1) Respect for and protection of the civilian population affected by the fighting. Civilians by definition play no active part in these conflicts and therefore cannot be the target of attacks. 2) Treat captured combatants and civilians humanely and provide adequate protection for them. 3) Report to the ICRC the identity of all prisoners and detainees and allow representatives of the ICRC to visit them according to the ICRC standards. 4) Collect, take care of and (treat surgically) and protect all the wounded at all times and places regardless of their affiliation. 5) I demand free access and guaranteed transit for eight convoys so that victims of the conflict may be treated without delay. Commander Tihomir Blaskic." Brigadier, are you familiar with this demand? This is not an order, this is a demand.

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: Yes, I am. It is a demand which I drafted myself, personally. Colonel Blaskic signed it and it bears the stamp of the Operative Zone and it is clear from it what the course of action is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Next document, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document D365, 365A for the French version and 356B for the English version.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This is dated 27 April, 1993, at 1020 hours. This is a supplement to the Order No. 01-4-560/93 of 24 April, 1993. If we look at it, this is the very order, actually the demand which we had just read. It was the Exhibit No. D364. And under one it says: "I prohibit any treatment of temporarily detained civilians which is contrary to the basic provisions of the Geneva Conventions." And it is signed commander, Tihomir Blaskic. Brigadier, do you remember this document and is this is a faithful copy of the original?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: Yes, this is a faithful copy of the original and it reflects the task given in this supplement order. This document was drafted by Colonel Blaskic personally and it was stamped at the Operative Zone command.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Next document, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document D366, 366A for the French version, 366B for the English version.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Brigadier, this is another document for which I believe we received from the Office of the Prosecutor. The copy is fairly illegible, but I will try to read the main points. This is an order by General Blaskic of 29 April from 1940 hours. And the subject heading is: "The release of detained civilians..." and then (it says something that is illegible). It is obviously addressed to a number of units whose names are not entirely legible."

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Excuse me, counsel. Again just to clarify the record, Mr. President. This is again, as you can see, there is no number on this document. This again is a document that was received from the Bosnian Croats, so when counsel says he received it from the Office of the Prosecutor, that's true. But we, in fact, received it from the Bosnian Croats. This is a document, I believe, that's been the subject of discussion prior to this time. But to clarify the record, I am sure counsel would want me to do that. We just want to put that on the record.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Yes, certainly. And let me also note that there is no registration number. But let me read it: "Under 1, General Blaskic orders that to immediately draft lists of detained civilians. And under 2, release all civilians (men, women, children) arrested during the conflict between the BH army and the HVO. And joint operative teams shall establish contact and commence clearing the battlefield i.e. the collection of the dead and their burial." And then we skip Item 4. "All released civilians must be guaranteed full safety in the locations in your zones of responsibility and you shall be held responsible for the situation in your zone of your responsibility." The rest is illegible. 5) "Immediate subordinate commanders and brigade commanders shall be responsible for the full execution of this order by 1000 hours on May 1, 1993. They must submit a written report with lists containing the following information." And then under 6) "In carrying out this order, cooperating with UNPROFOR, ICRC, UNHCR and the EU representatives." Signed by Commander Colonel Blaskic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: First of all, Brigadier, do you recognise Tihomir Blaskic's signature and the stamp?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: Yes, I recognise his signature. This document was drafted by Colonel Blaskic. It bears the stamp of the Operative Zone command. It was part of the cease-fire and the tasks which issued from the signed cease-fire agreement.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well, can we have the next document distributed, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document D367, 367A for the French version, 367B for the English version.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This is another order by Colonel Blaskic which we received from the Office of the Prosecutor. It is also barely legible in the Croatian original, at least in this light here. It has the subject heading, "Securing free passes for UNPROFOR forces." It is addressed to all the brigades, one through ten to the 4th military police battalion to the Vitezovi units and so on. The command says: "1) UNPROFOR and international humanitarian organisations shall be allowed free passage and access." Then the rest of the text is pretty legible. It is much better in the translation. But let me just ask you, Brigadier, do you recall this order? Do you remember the circumstances under which it was issued or do you not recall it?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: I do not see the signature on this document. The activities which were being implemented through the cease-fire agreement I know. And this would be one in a series of orders which would be part of the implementation and part of the tasks relating to the cease-fire. But I am not sure that I can really recall this order. It is not signed. And even this lettering, so I don't know, I don't think I can recall this order.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But look from the general look of it and the contents, could you say that this could have been written by General Blaskic?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: On the basis of its general look, it may have been issued by General Blaskic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Next document, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This is Document D368, 368A for the French version, 368B for the English version.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: An order by Colonel Blaskic of 31 May and this was typed over. It could be five or six. It could be May or June, '93. Time is 0945 hours. But if we look at the registration number, it is clear that it is May. It is addressed to the commanding officer of the 4th military police battalion and assistant for SIS. And subject heading says: "Actions contrary to the given orders and assignments." Order: "On 30 May, 1993, the officer on duty in the Central Bosnia Operative Zone informed me that Mr. Franjo Ramljak, and Mr. Slavko Hrgic, members of the military police, were forcibly expelling Muslim families. This was despite the order which banned such actions for which the above-named gentlemen are responsible. In order to prevent further actions that hinder the implementation of orders and the correct behaviour of military police members in carrying out their tasks, I hereby order: 1) Conduct an investigation into this case and take disciplinarian measures against the perpetrators in this incident. 2) Report to me explaining why, despite a number of warnings, certain members of your units are still causing such negative occurrences instead of protecting public order and suggest further actions to prevent such occurrences in the future. The deadline for the execution of this order is 5 June, 1993." Signed by commander, Colonel Tihomir Blaskic. Brigadier, do you recall this order?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: I do remember this event. The order was written and signed by Tihomir Blaskic and the stamp is that of the Operative Zone command.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In point 1, "Conduct an investigation into this case and take disciplinarian measures." How do you explain this? The commander of the military police is instructed to take disciplinarian measures.

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: I already said this previously that the commander of the Operative Zone did not have the authority to issue disciplinarian measures to the 4th military police battalion.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Colonel Blaskic is referring to a previous order in which he had forbidden forcible entrance into apartments, of civilians. Is that the order which we read about maybe about 20 minutes ago?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: Yes, that is that order that he was referring to here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. New document, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document D369, 369A for the French version, 369B for the English version.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Next document is from the Viteska Brigade. The date is 3 May, 1993. And Mario Cerkez orders to his subordinates: The subject heading is: "Prevention of forcible occupation of flats." "Order: It is forbidden for all members of the HVO units to enter by force in the houses and flats of families of Muslim nationality. All members of the HVO units are hereby ordered to IMMEDIATELY move out -- and immediately is capitalised -- to move out of the all forcibly occupied flats and houses and to inform the peoples' protection (the library building) about their moving out. Members of the HVO are also forbidden to exert any pressure on members of Muslim nationality to leave their flats and family houses. Any behaviour contrary to this order shall be regarded a criminal act and the perpetrators will be held accountable. The needs of the members of military units regarding their accommodation should be resolved through the command and to the competent civilian commission and a military housing commission. Brigade commander, Mario Cerkez." Brigadier, do you recognise the signature of Mario Cerkez?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: Yes, I recognise the signature of Mario Cerkez. I also know Mario Cerkez, Brigade commander. This document was drafted pursuant to an order issued by the Operative Zone commander.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Next document, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 370, 370A for the English version.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This is D370. This is the document which we received from the Office of the Prosecutor and I assume that this provenience the British battalion. And this is dated 16 June, 1993. It was addressed to all HVO brigades in the Central Bosnia Operative Zones and all other Central Bosnia Operative Zone independent units. It's a more comprehensive document. And No. 1: "Starting at 1200 hours on 18 June, 1993, cease all combat activities ( cease-fire) and freeze military activities, including troop movements, unit deployment and further fortification. Under 3) All units will give their full cooperation to the UNPROFOR in order to monitor the cessation of hostilities." And then skipping to 6) "Allow the delivery of humanitarian aid and freedom of movement and to the representatives of the international humanitarian organisations with the usual control procedures. 7) Do not use water, electricity or telephone lines as weapons. And make efforts to repair and maintain the facilities for water and electricity distribution." On the next page. Item 8) "Deliver all lists of prisoners of war and those killed in their areas and their exact location to the Central Bosnia Operative Zone and (Ljubomir Jurcic and his phone number). 9) All HVO units of these Central Bosnia Operative Zone are under an obligation to honour the Geneva Conventions of 12 and the month is illegible. And the month is illegible 1949. And the additional protocols, as well as other instruments of the laws of war and protection of human rights. Commander Tihomir Blaskic." Brigadier, do you recall this document? Do you recognise the signature?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: It is General Blaskic's signature. And the initials "FN" tell me that it was drafted by Franjo Nakic, who was the duty officer at the Operative Zone command. These are the tasks that were to be implemented and I remember them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Next document, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document D371, 371A for the English version. But these are two originals.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Mr. President, this document we received from the Prosecutor's office. There is an original document both in the English version and in the Croatian version, but as the original document in English is far more legible, I should like to ask my learned colleague, Mr. Hayman, to read it out to you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: "Vitez, June 19th, 1993. On the basis of the cease-fire agreement in the entire BiH, dated 10th June and 15th June, 1993, and the agreement with the other side to operationalise the agreement which is signed June 19th, 1993 in Vitez, I command: 1. To stop the arresting of civilians during the war actions in the form of imprisoning, taking hostages or illegal weakening of the enemy in all the cities and villages controlled by the HVO 3rd Operative Zone, middle Bosnia." 2. -- And here I'm going to ask Mr. Nobilo first to read the BSC, because the English doesn't follow. Can you read paragraph two, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: 2. "To stop the burning of facilities and the destruction of material property. Especially to protect sacred objects; that is to say the mosques, mejtefs, vakufs and mezars," or something of that nature, I can't quite read it.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Paragraph 3 continuing from the English exhibit D371A. "Every stealing and holding of the property shall be punished and solved through the military discipline measures and courts: 4. For the implementation of this command I make responsible all the brigade commanders and independent units commanders. They are to send customary reports on the implementation of the command." Signed Colonel Tihomir Blaskic, and a distribution list is given.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Mr. Hayman, please read again number two. It says "to enable the putting of houses and other objects on fire," to enable, not to forbid.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Mr. Nobilo read the Croatian version, which when properly translated means to stop. Whoever drafted this English original, shall we say, this perhaps was not their native tongue. But you're absolutely correct, the English version reads "I command to enable putting the houses and other objects on fire, as well as to enable destruction of other material goods."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: It goes into the other sentence.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: There it is, Your Honour. I think it's self explanatory.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: I suggest that we clarify this dilemma and place on the ELMO point 2, in large, so that our interpreters can translate the Croatian number 2 sentence. Let's have an enlargement on the ELMO, and then from the Croatian document the interpreters can read and translate. Therefore, Mr. President, I should like the interpreters to read out point 2 without my reading it. INTERPRETER: "To stop putting the houses and other objects on fire, as well as to stop the destruction of other material goods, and to enable special protection for sacred objects; mosques, mejtefs, vakufs and mezars."

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: I'd like to ask the interpreters to read out the word in yellow, highlighted in yellow, and it is omogucisti, to stop, to make impossible, prevent, to make impossible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: The point is whether it's negative or affirmative. According to the French interpreters, there are six syllables and a negation. It starts off with a negation. Not to enable, or to prevent. Is everyone in agreement? There is a negation coming in front of the word omogucisti, which means to prevent.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Let's move on to the next document.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Brigadier, before we go on to the next document, do you recognise the stamp and signature of Colonel Blaskic? Do you think that the document is authentic and a faithful copy of the original?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: Yes, it is a faithful copy of the original. I recognise General Blaskic's signature, but the stamp is not legible.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Something was added by hand with a black pen. Who wrote that?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: This is something that occurs frequently on documents, this is the handwriting of General Blaskic himself.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was General Blaskic able to speak English in 1993? Could he use the language?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: As far as I know, he did not have a knowledge of the English language, but we did have a translator, amateur translator, and in our correspondence with UNPROFOR we translated the documents from Croatian into English so that our correspondence with UNPROFOR should be as good as possible. But, however, I see that this was counterproductive in this particular case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 372, 372A for the English version.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Colonel Blaskic, on the 19th of June, 1993, at 1610 hours is writing to the commanders of the Viteska Brigade, the commanders of the Vitezovi special task force and the 4th military police battalion and police station. And he states in point 1 of his order: "To provide unobstructed passage for a convoy of food to the village of Kruscica on the 21st of June, 1993, which will be escorted by the UNHCR, the International Red Cross, and the European Monitoring Mission. 2. For the purpose of ensuring the passage of the food convoy, that the road be temporarily cleared of all anti-tank mines and other obstacles. 3. The delivery of the food convoy to the village of Kruscica is directly associated with supplying the town of Vitez with water from the Kruscica system. 4. The commander of the police station in Vitez shall be responsible for preventing any obstruction of the passage of the food convoy by citizens. 5. I shall hold the commanders of the Viteska Brigade, the Vitezovi special task force, the 4th military police battalion and the Vitez police station responsible for ensuring compliance with this order." Signed Colonel Blaskic. Do you recognise the document and the signature?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
utterances.text: The signature is that of General Blaskic. The activities contained in this order is something that I remember, so that I do remember the contents of that text.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The document was obtained from the office of the Prosecutor. May I have the next document, please?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document D373, 373A for the French version, 373B for the English version.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Therefore, we have an order from Colonel Blaskic on the 21st of June, 1993, sent to all the brigade commanders and to wardens of military prisons. The title is, "Relations to prisoners of war." "Based on the regulations of the Geneva Conventions of the 12th of August, 1949, which govern relations towards prisoners of war, I command:" The first point is relatively illegible. The translators tried to decipher it, but I wouldn't like to speculate, I would rather begin with point 2. "I forbid the use of prisoners of war for first labour on engineering projects on the territory. The shelter and trench cover-ups, roads, bunkers and villages. 3. Attention to be drawn to brigade commanders and military prison wardens, to the fact that using prisoners of war as a workforce for engineering projects on the territory constitutes a war crime, and that an international court for war crimes has been formed which will investigate and sanction such treatment. I hold responsible brigade commanders and wardens of military prisons for carrying out this order. Colonel Tihomir Blaskic." Brigadier, do you recognise the document, and the stamp and signature of Colonel Blaskic?

utterances.speaker: SLAVKO MARIN
